I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that fits my fields, my irrigation conditions, and the way I have farmed for many years. Since some people in my family work off-farm, I will keep the plan practical and not too labor-heavy. I will put 5 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 1.5 mu in cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough fertilizer for steady tillering and grain filling, irrigate a few times because I have well water, and use rotary tillage because it is efficient for me. For maize, I will use hybrid seed for better yield, apply more nitrogen than wheat, irrigate in key stages if water is available, and keep field work simple after wheat harvest. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it needs more management, but I will still grow it since I know the crop well. I will use improved seed, give moderate fertilizer, irrigate several times, and spray more often than for grain crops because insects are usually a bigger problem in cotton. My goal is stable yield, manageable labor, and lower risk across the year.
